title: Characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of a finite locally free module of constant rank
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ an integer, $M$ an $A$-module and $\varphi:M\to M$ an $A$-linear map, and assume that $M$ is *finite locally free of constant rank $n$*: there are $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that for each $i$ the localization $M_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] is a free module of rank $n$ (isomorphic to $(A_{f_i})^{n}$) over the localized ring $A_{f_i}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For a ring map $A\to A'$ write $M\otimes_AA'$ and $\varphi_{A'}=\varphi\otimes1$ for the base change [def-weil-module-base-change]; when $M\otimes_AA'$ is free of rank $n$ over $A'$, $\det(T\cdot1-\varphi_{A'})\in A'[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] denotes the determinant [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] of the $A'[T]$-linear endomorphism $T\cdot1-\varphi_{A'}\otimes1$ of the free $A'[T]$-module $(M\otimes_AA')\otimes_{A'}A'[T]$; concretely, if $(a_{jk})\in M_n(A')$ [def-weil-matrix] is the matrix of $\varphi_{A'}$ in a basis of $M\otimes_AA'$, it is $\det(T\,I_n-(a_{jk}))$, independent of the basis. The image of $P=\sum_kc_kT^k\in A[T]$ in $A'[T]$ is $\sum_k\bar c_kT^k$, $\bar c_k$ the image of $c_k$. The *characteristic polynomial* $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi:M\to M)\in A[T]$ is the unique polynomial $\chi\in A[T]$ such that for every ring map $A\to A'$ with $M\otimes_AA'$ free of rank $n$ over $A'$, the image of $\chi$ in $A'[T]$ is $\det(T\cdot1-\varphi_{A'})$; it exists and is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence], and it has the form $T^n+c_{n-1}T^{n-1}+\dots+c_0$ with $c_k\in A$ by the same lemma. It depends only on $A$, $M$ and $\varphi$: not on the choice of $f_1,\dots,f_r$, and not on $n$ (if $A\neq0$ the rank $n$ is determined by $M$; if $A=0$ then $A[T]=0$). If $M$ is itself free of rank $n$, $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi)$ is the usual characteristic polynomial $\det(T\cdot1-\varphi)$ (take $A'=A$).

proof.text: *The polynomial exists and is unique.* The hypotheses of the definition ($A$, $n$, $M$, $\varphi$, and $f_1,\dots,f_r$ generating the unit ideal with $M_{f_i}\cong(A_{f_i})^n$) are exactly those of [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence], which gives exactly one $\chi\in A[T]$ with the characterizing property (for every $A\to A'$ with $M\otimes_AA'$ free of rank $n$, the image of $\chi$ in $A'[T]$ is $\det(T\cdot1-\varphi_{A'})$), and gives $\chi=T^n+c_{n-1}T^{n-1}+\dots+c_0$. So the definition names one polynomial, and the monic form is that lemma's 'moreover' clause, not a claim of the definition. The determinant on the right is well defined: $M\otimes_AA'\cong A'^n$ makes $(M\otimes_AA')\otimes_{A'}A'[T]\cong A'[T]^n$ free with a finite basis, so [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] applies over the commutative ring $A'[T]$, and it does not depend on the basis (matrices in two bases are conjugate). The free case is the specialization $A'=A$, $A\to A$ the identity, for which $M\otimes_AA=M$ and the image of $\chi$ is $\chi$.

proof.text: *Independence of $f_1,\dots,f_r$.* Let $g_1,\dots,g_s\in A$ be a second family generating the unit ideal with $M_{g_j}$ free of rank $n$, and let $\chi$, $\chi'$ be the polynomials step 1 gives for $(f_i)$ and for $(g_j)$. The characterizing property quantifies over ring maps $A\to A'$ with $M\otimes_AA'$ free of rank $n$ and does not mention the family. So $\chi$ has the property, and the uniqueness of [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] applied with the family $(g_j)$ gives $\chi=\chi'$.

Localizing the isomorphism $M_{f_i}\cong(A_{f_i})^n$ further at $g_j$ gives $M_h\cong(A_h)^n$ (as $(M_{f_i})_{g_j}=M_h$ by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]), and in the same way $M_h\cong(A_h)^{n'}$. Hence the integer $n$ is determined by $M$ when $A

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 09XI, proof of (3)=>(1), last paragraph (CharPol_A defined by gluing matrix characteristic polynomials over a standard covering, details omitted). The definition takes its data from lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence (existence, uniqueness, monic of degree n). Statement made self-contained: localizations M_f and A_f, base change M (x)_A A', polynomial ring, determinant over A'[T] of the base-changed endomorphism (matrix form, basis-independent) and the coefficientwise image A[T] -> A'[T] now named with their nodes (stmt_deps added: def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-module-base-change, def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-endomorphism-determinant, def-weil-matrix). Three proof steps record well-posedness: (1) existence/uniqueness and the monic form from the existence lemma, and the determinant being defined; (2) independence of f_1..f_r from uniqueness (the characterizing property does not mention them); (3) independence of n, which the notation CharPol_A(phi) drops and the users (direct-sum lemma, idempotent splitting) never fix: n is determined by M when A != 0 (common localization A_{f_i g_j} != 0 at a maximal ideal, invariant basis number), and A[T]=0 when A=0. Free case noted (A'=A). Mathlib re-searched three ways: LinearMap.charpoly exists for free finite modules only; nothing for projective or locally free modules. The source repository has no locally free characteristic polynomial.
